person: Beverly Shaw is a 72-year-old retired fourth-grade teacher in Roanoke, Virginia, who keeps her receipts in a shoebox and her card statements in a folder. Her grandson set up Athena and her email, and she has been wary of it since someone took $800 from her checking account through the payment app last spring. She has a handful of class action notices in her email and has never filed one, partly because she worries the whole thing is a scam. She wants everything explained plainly before it happens, and she wants to be able to stop it.
stated_up_front: Hello, I'm sorry, I'm not very good with these things. My grandson said you could help me with some settlement notices in my email, but I'd like you to tell me what you're going to do before you do anything, please.

facts.about: Her email address and which account her notices arrive in
facts.truth: Her Gmail account, where about a dozen settlement notices have collected since spring.
A Blue Ridge Credit Union Visa; she keeps paper statements in a blue folder going back to 2022.

facts.about: Whether she has bought small appliances online
facts.truth: Yes. She ordered an air fryer in March 2023 for $79.99 and two electric kettles, one for herself and one for her sister, in 2024.
She will sign a claim only for something she is sure she bought, because the form says it is under penalty of perjury and that frightens her.

facts.about: A settlement she opted out of
facts.truth: She remembers mailing back an exclusion form for a coffee settlement, because her late husband liked that brand and she did not want to be part of the case.
She filed a rice cooker claim herself with her grandson's help in the summer and has the confirmation email.
She bought headphones on a trip to Toronto in 2024 to visit her cousin, paying with the same Visa.
She received an email from a payout desk asking for a $4.95 fee and her bank login; she did not click it and wants to be told if it is real.
Her daughter Carol calls every Sunday and asks if she has done anything about the bank; Beverly does not want to tell her she lost more money.
Her grandson Ethan is on the phone most evenings and can be asked if she is unsure of a screen.

unknowns: What the class period is for each settlement, and whether her purchases fall inside it.
Whether any of her earlier purchases appear under a hardware store's name on her card statement instead of the product's brand.
The deadline for each settlement, other than what the notice email says in print.
Whether a claim can be withdrawn after she signs it.
